name: WebWeaver

paper.title: WebWeaver: Structuring Web-Scale Evidence with Dynamic Outlines for Open-Ended Deep Research

construction.unit: evidence-bank entry per visited URL (goal, summary, evidence) + an outline whose sections cite entry ids
construction.kept_as: LLM-extracted evidence passages (asked to keep original wording) + LLM summary
construction.processing: web search → LLM picks URLs → page read (≤24k tokens) → LLM extracts summary and evidence; planner rewrites the cited outline
construction.writer: gpt-oss-120b (URL selection, summary, evidence); planner LLM (outline)

organization.structure: flat id-keyed evidence bank + hierarchical outline citing ids
organization.stores: memory bank (url → goal, summary, evidence); outline
organization.index: sequential ids <id_n> per URL; no embeddings

management.operations: append entries for new URLs (seen URLs reused); outline rewritten in each cycle

retrieval.query: writer names the ids cited under the current section
retrieval.candidates: bank entries with those ids (exact lookup)
retrieval.selection: writer LLM, guided by the outline citations
retrieval.budget: retrieved evidence cut at 20,000 characters per call; writer context cap 100k tokens

use.context: outline + goal and summary of every page + the current section's evidence; earlier evidence masked
use.reasoning: section-by-section ReAct writing (~25 steps per report)

classify.note: The bank itself is a flat append-only list keyed by id; the structure is the agent-written outline, which is rewritten each cycle and routes the writer to ids.

stages.ingestion: The planner issues batches of web queries; a search API returns the top 10 results per query, an LLM picks relevant URLs from titles and snippets, and each page is read and cut to 24k tokens.
stages.construction: An LLM (gpt-oss-120b) turns each page into a short query-focused summary and longer evidence (quotes, data, tables); summary and evidence are stored under a new <id_n> in the memory bank.
stages.organization: The bank is a flat list keyed by id. The planner keeps a hierarchical outline and cites bank ids under each subsection; only summaries enter the planner's own context.
stages.update: After new evidence arrives the planner rewrites the whole outline (expand, restructure, add citations); on average 2.2 outline rounds per task.
stages.retrieval: The writer walks the outline section by section, calling retrieve with the cited ids to pull those entries' evidence from the bank.
stages.answer: The writer reads the outline, every page's summary and the current section's evidence, writes the section, and the evidence is masked before the next section.
stages.learning: WebWeaver-3k (3.3k planning and 3.1k writing trajectories from a teacher) is used for full fine-tuning of Qwen3-30B-A3B.

summary: Deep-research agent whose memory is an id-keyed evidence bank plus a dynamic outline that cites it: the planner interleaves search with outline rewriting, and the writer composes section by section from only the evidence each section cites.
notes: DESIGN: paper §2 (actions, memory bank), §3.2-3.3, §4.1, Tables 3-4; code DeepResearch repo WebAgent/WebWeaver at f72f75d8 (2026-02-27). Venue: only arXiv v1-v3 known (v3 2025-10-07); arXiv comment 'An agent system for open-ended deep research'. Not a conversational memory system: the 'memory' is per-task working memory for one report. learning=mixed because the framework is prompt-only but the paper also SFTs a 30B model on WebWeaver-3k.

sources.code_note: The WebWeaver folder was added to the Alibaba-NLP/DeepResearch repo on 2026-02-26 (commit 330a5bf2) and patched the next day (f72f75d8, pinned here), about five months after arXiv v3. Its scripts default to qwen3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507 for planner and writer, while the paper's default is Claude-sonnet-4; the summary model is any local vLLM model. Exact identity with the paper's runs is not guaranteed.

headline: The bank stores LLM-extracted evidence per URL, not the raw page; the planner only ever sees the short summaries.
The writer is not limited to cited evidence: its first prompt already holds every page's goal and summary; the retrieve call adds full evidence for the ids a section cites.
After each written section its evidence is masked from the context, so the writer's context stays near one section's evidence.

open_questions: The brute-force baseline changes two things at once (whole bank in context and no per-section retrieval), so the gain cannot be split between focused context and outline-guided citation.
The outline-round study uses only tasks that ran three rounds and compares their own intermediate outlines, so it does not show what a one-round policy would score on all tasks.

discussion.takeaway: For long web-research reports, keep gathered evidence out of the model's context in an id-keyed bank, let an outline that is rewritten as evidence arrives decide which ids each section needs, and write one section at a time. This gives the paper's best DeepResearch Bench, DeepConsult and DeepResearchGym scores, notably 93.37% citation accuracy.

claims.claim: State of the art on open-ended deep research.
claims.evidence: DRB RACE 50.62 (Qwen3-235B) and 50.58 (Claude-sonnet-4) vs 49.71 Gemini-2.5-pro deep research; DeepConsult win 66.86%; DRGym avg 96.77 vs 96.02. Tables 1-2

claims.claim: Outline-guided, per-section retrieval raises citation accuracy.
claims.evidence: C. acc. 93.37 vs 78.30 (Gemini) and 75.01 (OpenAI); 86.73 with the brute-force writer. Table 1, Fig. 10

claims.claim: Iterative outline optimization improves reports and outlines.
claims.evidence: DRB overall 48.15 → 49.55 over three rounds; outline judge score 81.9 → 92.3 (DRB), 77.2 → 88.2 (DRGym). Figs. 6-9

claims.claim: Section-wise writing beats writing from the whole bank.
WebWeaver-3k SFT teaches a small model the workflow.
claims.evidence: Qwen3-30B-A3B citation accuracy 25.00 → 85.90, DRGym 77.27 → 90.89, DeepConsult 4.57 → 6.09. Fig. 14

discussion.limits_src: The paper has no limitations section.
reading: The 'memory' is per-task working memory for one report, filled from the web; there is no long-term or cross-task memory, so it is not comparable with conversational memory systems.
The writer's first prompt contains every page's summary (about 15k tokens on DRB), so each section is written with the whole summary set in view, not only its cited evidence.
The brute-force ablation removes both focused context and id-based retrieval at once.
In the outline-round study readability drops slightly on DRB (48.73 → 48.58) and clarity on DRGym (91.36 → 90.42) at round 3; the gains are in comprehensiveness, insight and support.
The text reports DRGym support 90.95 → 98.73 for brute-force vs hierarchical, while Fig. 11 labels the brute-force bar 91.82.
Proprietary baselines on DRB are copied from the leaderboard; whether the DeepConsult and DRGym baseline rows were rerun is not stated.
Released code (Feb 2026) defaults to Qwen3-235B for planner and writer, not the paper's Claude-sonnet-4.

abstract.text: WebWeaver targets open-ended deep research, where an agent must turn hundreds of web pages into a long, cited report. A planner alternates between web search and rewriting an outline, and every visited page is reduced to a summary and extracted evidence stored under an id in a memory bank that the outline cites. A writer then composes the report section by section, retrieving only the evidence cited for each section and dropping it afterwards. The system reports state-of-the-art results on DeepResearch Bench, DeepConsult and DeepResearchGym, and a 3k-trajectory SFT set lets a 30B model learn the workflow.
